question: My lab report came back and my doctor started me on a new blood pressure medicine. What do these kidney numbers mean, and can I keep taking ibuprofen for my back pain?
private_situation: Marcus Whitfield, a patient at Larkspur Family Health, has stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 52, potassium 5.4) and was just started on lisinopril, and he takes ibuprofen for back pain.
answer_rubric: Explains that eGFR 52 indicates moderately reduced kidney function (CKD stage 3a)
Warns that NSAIDs such as ibuprofen can harm kidneys and interact with lisinopril (and raise potassium)
Mentions the elevated potassium (5.4) and why it matters with an ACE inhibitor
Suggests safer alternatives or asking the doctor or pharmacist before continuing ibuprofen
